source.title: Towards Task and Architecture-Independent Generalization Gap Predictors
source.authors: Scott Yak; J. Gonzalvo; Hanna Mazzawi

record.file_problem: Text contains the full paper, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether margin-signature features predict generalization gaps across tasks and architectures, using a different set of models and synthetic data; it does not test any listed version directly.
record.gate_note: The reported predictor scores and margin-signature analyses are the paper's own results. Discussion of prior work is not extracted as a result.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates margin-based predictors of generalization gaps on synthetic spiral datasets. It does not measure magnitude-aware weight sharpness or test any other listed version. Varying optimizer, width, dropout and batch size in the training pool does not itself establish the comparisons those versions require.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate when restricted to the tested spiral datasets and fully connected architectures. The authors conclude that aggregated margin features enable task-independent gap prediction and that DNN and RNN predictors outperform linear predictors on almost every prediction task; cross-dataset performance is substantially weaker than dataset-dependent performance.
record.recipe_differences: Uses margin-signature regression on synthetic spiral datasets and fully connected networks; studies prediction of the gap rather than the generalization interventions or measurements in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Predictor performance varies with dataset-dependent versus dataset-independent training and with same-distribution, unseen-hyperparameter, and unseen-dataset evaluation. In the appendix, high dropout and high learning rate correlate with lower accuracy and lower gap predictions; batch normalization and batch size show no clear direct correlation.

fits_no_version.finding: Margin-signature regressors predict generalization gaps on synthetic spiral tasks. Dataset-dependent R² ranges from 0.945 to 0.965; the recorded single-model results range from 0.338 to 0.584.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Margin signatures can predict generalization gaps across sampled fully connected architectures and spiral tasks, with substantially weaker prediction across datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix C reports that high dropout and learning rates correlate with lower training accuracy and smaller predicted gaps; batch size and batch normalization show no clear direct gap correlation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this sampled spiral-network pool, some training hyperparameters correlate with training accuracy and generalization gaps, without establishing their effects on held-out accuracy.

record.peer_reviewed: ICML 2019 Workshop on Understanding and Improving Generalization in Deep Learning
record.problems: The experiments use synthetic spiral datasets and fully connected feed-forward networks. The predictor scores are averaged over 5-fold cross-validation, but no error bars or significance tests are reported. The number of trained networks is stated as up to 13,500 because networks with diverging losses were discarded.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Table 1 reports the R² and L1 loss for each predictor and task, but the extraction prioritizes R² and omits the separate L1-loss metrics. Test-accuracy-prediction results in Appendix B do not measure the generalization gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training.
Test-error trends beyond the width needed for zero training error; sampled widths are not analyzed this way.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out performance of adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets; no optimizer comparison is reported.
Large-batch held-out penalties under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations. Training uses fixed steps; Appendix C discusses gap correlations rather than the required held-out comparison.
Whether adding dropout lowers held-out error. Appendix C associates high dropout with lower training accuracy and smaller gaps, which does not establish improved test accuracy.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm and margin measures. Margin signatures alone do not test this comparison.
Retraining after removing memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 also contains unrecorded single-model unseen-hyperparameter R² values of 0.384, 0.487 and 0.527 for linear, DNN and RNN predictors. These are additional method-performance results, not missing evidence for a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and natural-label generalization.
Test error as network width passes the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers on the listed benchmarks.
Large- versus small-batch generalization under the listed training recipes.
The effect of adding dropout on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
The effect of removing memorized training examples.
